question: How to assign a fixed number of party workers across regions in different population / preference scenarios (aligned, swing, antagonistic regions)

definitions.roles: from round-0 TRUE regional mean P under the world's ORACLE manifesto: aligned = max, antagonistic = min, swing = of the remaining two the one with |P − 0.5| smallest, other = last; ties by lower region index
definitions.splits: largest remainder; equal remainders go to the larger region (aligned before swing for aligned_swing)
definitions.delta_vs_none: E(arm) − E(none) in the same world and streams
definitions.d_support_by_role: final regional mean P (arm) − final regional mean P (none), region by role
definitions.d_e_contribution_by_role: (n_r/N)·ΔP_r; the four roles sum to delta_vs_none
definitions.converts_by_role: voters converted by the IC cascade over the game, by region (observer hook)
definitions.converts_outside_target_share: share of converts outside the regions that received workers
definitions.posthoc_largest_region: default scenario split by the role of the largest region

test_families: per scenario × K: 6 arms vs none + 15 pairwise between arms (21), Wilcoxon on E and exact McNemar on wins, Holm within the family
deviations: Parity uses x_parity.parity_rel (x_common.parity_check with tolerance max(0.01, 3·SE, 5% of the mean), as in X4), because CPU and GPU draw different random numbers.
Per-region converts come from run_batch's observer hook (the per-round converted mask); no library change.
With K = 4 and near-equal regions, 'even' and 'proportional' give the same 1/1/1/1 split in most worlds (identical games).

parity.cell: default scenario: none, K = 4 all→swing, K = 10 even
